 Matt Renshaw with a filthy delivery which Joe Root attempts to reverse sweep. Josh Inglis appeals, but the umpire responds by signalling a wide.
 Root repeats the shot next delivery - gets a bit of glove on it - but Inglis is nowhere near it.
 A couple of balls later, Tom Banton bisects the fielders at cover and mid-off to jab a four. Nicely played.

 Tom Banton is a dangerous player. He made his name playing in the middle against spin but in the last year or so, he's really proven he can hit the seamers too.

 Eng 113-1 published at 20 overs 20 overs 
 Tom Banton emphatically pulled seamer Riley Meredith for four in the previous over, but is a little more circumspect against Adam Zampa.
 After he and Joe Root rotate the strike with singles for the first three balls, Banton decides to shoulder arms to a delivery from the leg-spinner which whizzes wide of his off stump.
 5 1 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 108-1 published at 19 overs 19 overs 
 Image source, Getty Images Just on sandpapergate, Chadd Sayers, the former Aussie international who was a reserve fast bowler during the infamous 2018 series in South Africa, has been speaking to Australian broadcaster SEN.
 "I'm comfortable sitting here right now and where I was in the situation that I believe that everyone in that side knew what was going on and what was being used," he said.
 Sayers has completely verified the idea that sandpaper was used in the second Test in Port Elizabeth, says more than three people knew, and that there was a meeting of "60-90 minutes" to discuss collective responsibility. 
 This all comes after Pat Cummins' denials.
 No signs of a lid being put back on this can of worms anytime soon.

 Adam Zampa's arm ball strikes Joe Root on the pad, and he appeals.
 However, the Aussie leg-spinner is a lone voice at the Adelaide Oval. That was sliding down leg and there's not much interest among his team-mates.
 Root and Tom Banton knock Zampa into the gaps for four singles as England reach three figures.

 Riley Meredith bangs it in short, quick and manages to find some movement. Joe Root responds by trying an audacious uppercut, but ends up being surprised and is knocked off his feet.
 Root got some bat on it, picks up a couple of runs after some average fielding by Spencer Johnson down at fine leg, before chuckling to himself.

 We saw early on in Perth that the ball was hitting the splice of the bat and they weren't timing it. It's a less bouncy pitch that will suit the England players a lot more.
 They should be able to get a decent score on this type of pitch against this kind of attack in these conditions - and they've made a decent start.
